meta.title: Superpowers Review
meta.source_of_truth_rule: When docs and code disagree, prefer current code and current migrations as implementation truth.

overall_assessment.summary: The product direction is coherent, but the current codebase is still a seeded prototype. The main gaps are backend trust, crew/invite integrity, zone-control correctness, feature/spec mismatch, and test drift.
highest_priority_themes: Replace multi-step client mutations with transactional RPCs
Fix zone-control correctness before adding more game features
Align spec claims with what the app actually does today

findings.title: Competitive game mutations are still too client-trusting
findings.summary: Authenticated clients can still bypass intended server-controlled game flows.

evidence.note: place_tag_scored accepts p_user_id from the client and does not verify auth.uid().
users table still allows direct client profile updates.
tags table still allows direct client inserts.

impact: Potential user impersonation in RPCs
Possible rule bypass via direct table writes
Competitive integrity is not credible under adversarial clients
recommendations: Make scored placement derive identity from auth.uid() instead of p_user_id.
Remove direct client insert access to tags.
Restrict users.update to safe profile fields or move writes behind RPCs.

findings.title: Crew creation and join flows are non-atomic and invite security is too broad
findings.summary: Crew membership and invite usage are orchestrated by multi-step client writes with broad RLS permissions.

evidence.note: createCrew performs separate crew insert, crew_members insert, and users update.
joinCrew performs separate invite read, crew_members insert, users update, and invite update.
Users can insert themselves into crew_members.
Any authenticated user can look up invites.
Any authenticated user can update invite use_count.

impact: Partial failures can leave inconsistent membership state
Invite usage is race-prone
Invite abuse surface is larger than intended
recommendations: Replace create/join/leave crew flows with transactional RPCs.
Remove direct client crew_members inserts.
Only mutate invite usage inside a server-side join RPC.

findings.title: New crew member_count is likely wrong
findings.summary: A new crew appears to start at member_count = 1 and then gets incremented again when the founder is inserted into crew_members.

evidence.note: crews.member_count default is 1.
Crew member count trigger increments on insert.

impact: Incorrect crew stats on creation
Potential leaderboard and UI inaccuracies
recommendations: Initialize member_count at 0 and let trigger/RPC own the count.
Prefer a single transactional source of truth for denormalized counters.

findings.title: Zone-control trigger has a correctness bug and misses spec tie-break logic
findings.summary: Zone flip events can fail when no valid actor exists, and tie-breaking does not match the design spec.

evidence.note: Trigger inserts a zone_flipped event with a fallback actor_id of 00000000-....
activity_feed.actor_id is non-null and a foreign key.
Spec says ties are broken by most recent tag timestamp.
Trigger chooses max count from jsonb without implementing recency tie-break.

impact: Decay or edge-case zone transitions can break feed writes
Zone ownership can be nondeterministic and diverge from the spec
recommendations: Compute winners from tag rows, not unordered JSON only.
Implement explicit recency tie-break logic.
Use a real system actor or allow nullable actor_id for system-generated events.

findings.title: Solo-play implementation does not match the solo-crew design
findings.summary: The spec says solo players are effectively one-person crews, but the implementation still has a true no-crew state.

evidence.note: Spec says solo players are mechanically identical to crews.
App still exposes a real no-crew screen.
Tags use v_user.crew_id and can therefore be crewless.
Zone tag_counts exclude crew_id is null.

impact: Crewless users can tag but not participate under equal territory rules
Product claims and schema semantics disagree
recommendations: Either auto-create one-person crews on signup or remove the solo-crew claim from the spec.

findings.title: Organic zone expansion is promised but not implemented
findings.summary: The current app only works with pre-existing seeded zones.

evidence.note: Spec says new zones should be generated when tagging outside existing zones.
Placement only looks up an existing zone.
Playable territory is currently pre-seeded.

impact: The map does not truly expand
Exploration-first claims are overstated
The app is city-seed dependent
recommendations: If zone generation is MVP, implement it server-side now.
If not, downgrade the spec to a seeded-city MVP.

findings.title: Map and realtime architecture is not shaped for scale or proximity-based UX
findings.summary: Map/feed loading is global and reload-heavy rather than bounded by viewport or radius.

evidence.note: get_tags_for_map returns all active tags.
loadMapData fetches all zones, tags, and crews.
Realtime change handlers trigger full reloads.
Nearby sorts the full tag list client-side.
Feed is a global latest-50 query.

impact: Poor scaling as tag volume grows
Mismatch with spec's nearby/proximity framing
Unnecessary server and client work on each realtime change
recommendations: Bound map queries by viewport or radius.
Separate global feed from nearby feed explicitly.
Apply incremental realtime updates where possible.

findings.title: The app does not yet deliver the claimed AR loop
findings.summary: Current implementation is camera-assisted placement, not a real nearby-tag AR overlay experience.

evidence.note: Spec says nearby tags should appear overlaid in camera view.
Current camera screen is camera feed plus HUD only.
Tag placement never passes goOverTagId.
Tag details expose no contest/report actions.

impact: AR differentiator is overstated
Contesting/reporting loops are incomplete in UI
recommendations: Reframe current state as GPS + camera placement MVP until actual overlay behavior exists.
Add explicit report/contest affordances if they are part of MVP.

findings.title: Anti-cheat and rate limiting are named in docs but not materially implemented
findings.summary: The schema has a last_tagged_at column, but the placement path does not use it and there is no visible anti-spoof logic.

evidence.note: Research says anti-cheat from day 1 is critical.
Spec references movement checks and device attestation.
Rate-limit column exists.
Placement updates XP/spray but does not enforce last_tagged_at or cooldowns.

impact: Spam and spoof abuse remain open
The most important category risk is still largely unaddressed
recommendations: Implement minimum viable cooldowns and movement sanity checks inside placement RPCs.
Downgrade anti-cheat claims in docs until real controls exist.

findings.title: Architecture story is inconsistent across spec and plans
findings.summary: Docs disagree about whether core game logic lives in Edge Functions, direct client writes, or Postgres RPCs.

evidence.note: Spec says server logic uses Supabase Edge Functions.
AR plan says client queries PostGIS and inserts tags directly before scored validation exists.
Scoring plan moves core logic into Postgres functions via RPC.

impact: Creates planning ambiguity
Makes it easier for implementation and docs to diverge
recommendations: Pick one authoritative mutation architecture and rewrite docs accordingly.
For MVP, Postgres RPC + strict RLS is the simplest coherent choice.

findings.title: Doc, code, and test drift is already visible
findings.summary: Jest passes, but TypeScript fails due stale integration-test assumptions.

evidence.note: Test file still carries stale assumptions around decay naming and shapes.
Zone-control tests reference stale event naming/assumptions.
Generated types do not match what the failing tests still expect.

impact: Passing Jest gives a false sense of stability
The repo can drift faster than docs and tests are being updated
recommendations: Make npx tsc --noEmit a hard gate.
Fix stale integration tests before expanding scope.
Regenerate database types after migration changes.

findings.title: Project documentation is still partially template-level
findings.summary: The repo README is still the default Expo template instead of actual project setup and architecture documentation.

evidence.note: README still contains default Expo starter content.

impact: Poor contributor onboarding
Weakens the stated goal of building for a maintainable multi-contributor future
recommendations: Replace README with real setup, local Supabase, testing, and architecture instructions.

spec_code_disagreements.doc_claim: Core game logic is in Edge Functions.
spec_code_disagreements.current_code_reality: Core scoring is in Postgres RPCs and the older AR plan still describes direct client-side validation/inserts.
spec_code_disagreements.recommended_resolution: Standardize on Postgres RPCs + RLS for MVP and update docs to match.

spec_code_disagreements.doc_claim: Solo players are one-person crews with the same mechanics.
spec_code_disagreements.current_code_reality: The app supports a true no-crew state and null crew_id tags do not count for zone control.
spec_code_disagreements.recommended_resolution: Either auto-create solo crews or remove the solo-crew claim.

spec_code_disagreements.doc_claim: Zones expand organically when users tag outside existing zones.
spec_code_disagreements.current_code_reality: No zone creation path exists; current gameplay depends on seeded zones.
spec_code_disagreements.recommended_resolution: Implement server-side zone creation or downgrade spec to seeded-city MVP.

spec_code_disagreements.doc_claim: Nearby tags appear as camera overlays in AR view.
spec_code_disagreements.current_code_reality: Current camera screen is a HUD over camera feed without nearby tag overlay logic.
spec_code_disagreements.recommended_resolution: Reframe current state as camera-assisted placement until overlay logic exists.

spec_code_disagreements.doc_claim: Anti-cheat from day 1 with movement checks and device attestation.
spec_code_disagreements.current_code_reality: No meaningful anti-cheat is visible in the current placement path.
spec_code_disagreements.recommended_resolution: Implement minimal anti-abuse now or reduce the strength of the claim.

recommended_next_actions.action: Lock down RLS and trust boundaries
recommended_next_actions.reason: Without this, every higher-level game system is easy to bypass.

recommended_next_actions.action: Convert crew create/join/leave into transactional RPCs
recommended_next_actions.reason: Current client-orchestrated writes are inconsistent and too permissive.
Zone control is core gameplay and currently has bug/spec issues.

recommended_next_actions.action: Implement real placement cooldowns using last_tagged_at
recommended_next_actions.reason: Basic anti-spam belongs in MVP for a location game.

recommended_next_actions.action: Decide whether solo users are real crews
recommended_next_actions.reason: The product and schema currently disagree on a central mechanic.

recommended_next_actions.action: Decide whether organic zone generation is in MVP
recommended_next_actions.reason: Current implementation does not support the claim.

recommended_next_actions.action: Fix stale integration tests and enforce TypeScript clean builds
recommended_next_actions.reason: Current green tests are misleading because tsc still fails.

recommended_next_actions.action: Replace template README with real contributor docs
recommended_next_actions.reason: The repo is missing basic operational documentation.

suggested_prompt_for_next_llm.goal: Use this review as the primary critique of the current Graffiti app and superpowers docs. Prioritize actions that secure the backend and align the spec with actual implementation.
instructions: Treat findings F1, F2, F4, F6, F7, F9, and F11 as highest priority.
When docs and code disagree, prefer current migrations and current code.
Do not assume the AR, solo-crew, anti-cheat, or organic-zone claims are already implemented.
If proposing a roadmap, put security and transactional integrity ahead of feature expansion.

checks_run.details: 0 errors, 9 warnings, warnings confined to tests
Integration tests still reference stale RPC/status/type assumptions
